recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-5673; any future clarification for 'with every meal' versus scheduled meal-time dosing should be handled under a separate Jira/work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-5673 was a Published FHIR-core datatypes change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that Timing support instructions such as "with meals". The issue proposed optional duration/unit fields with a unit-required invariant and meal event codes, and its final resolution points to FHIR-3841.
initial_application: FHIR-3841, the referenced Published/Persuasive with Modification Timing restructure, was applied historically in git-svn commit db55db7414cc49a9bd93c668c9fd19c3de26fccf, whose subject includes '#3841: restructure timing'. Current source/datatypes/timing.xml retains the relevant application: optional duration and durationUnit, a durationUnit invariant, Timing.repeat.when bound to EventTiming, and EventTiming meal codes C, CM, CD, and CV.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Timing as an active datatype and marks it normative. Later FHIR-8697 added offset and before/after-meal support without removing the base meal codes. A 2023 Zulip implementers thread clarified that Timing meal codes are for scheduled meal-time timing; truly 'every meal' trigger/precondition semantics may be represented differently and would require a separate decision if the work group wants new guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The latest combined branch already contains the build-scope Timing source needed to express 'with meals' as repeat.when=C or a specific meal code, plus the duration/durationUnit invariant from the referenced Timing restructure.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-5673's final resolution explicitly points to this broader Timing restructure, which introduced the relevant Timing.repeat.when and EventTiming support.
